lesson.subtitle: Lesson 3 -- Could You Say That Again?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fernanda Bassani Rubio | Lesson 3 -- Could You Say That Again?
lesson.grammar_point: can and could for polite requests

listenings.text: Hello, Fernanda, this is Li from the quality team in Shanghai. I am calling about the samples for your customer. We have a new shipment ready. There are twelve boxes of samples. They leave the plant tomorrow, and the customer can test them next Wednesday. Sorry, I know I speak fast. If you have a question, please send it in writing, and I can answer tonight. And could you confirm by email that the customer address is correct? It is the same address as last time. Thank you very much. Bye.

I work on global projects, and on my calls there are people from six or seven countries. Do I understand everything? No. Nobody does. Every accent is different. So I have a simple rule. When I do not catch something, I ask immediately. I say: sorry, could you repeat that, please? I never wait ten minutes, because then I am lost. For names and numbers, I always ask people to write them in the chat. At the end, I confirm the important points: so, the delivery is on Friday, right? People never think this is strange. They think it is professional.
